## ORACLE-126 — Unit 17 certificate fixture basis, symbols and cumulative registry

Classification: CERTIFICATE_ORACLE / LOCAL_ATTAINMENT_FIXTURE, with separate finite
GLOBAL_REFERENCE rows. Authority is DESIGN 4.14 and TEST_PLAN 39/40 (CE1–CE20),
remotely closed at 2cc8bd16287a3ec6a192c4f0b9249ded73484b99, tree
d418d019ddbb470531b4a8e95faca10c1ea4f264. No authority, CONTRACT, SPEC_LOCK, production,
consuming test, independent production checker or CONFORMANCE change occurs here.
Only this catalogue is amended. The pre-amendment catalogue and all
its classifications/registries remain byte-for-byte intact; numbering is additive.

Source basis: pinned V2.2 def:instance, ass:active, def:parameter/eq:compact-density;
lem:interval; lem:empty and lem:unit (both complete proofs); prop:endpoints and its
monotonicity proof; sec:global complete reconstruction table, alg:global,
prop:global-invariant and proofs. The private package records exact hashes and TeX
line ranges. Read the Unit 16-closed sources, not Unit 15 historical telemetry text.

Rows are governing human fixtures, not production output. A private JSON companion
is an exact mirror only. Cells are Python literals read by literal_eval, never eval.
Tuples/lists fingerprint identically as compact ASCII-escaped JSON arrays. Each row
is encoded in printed order with separators comma/colon and a single LF, concatenated,
then SHA-256 hashed. This is the same U15/U16 row-payload convention; retain both old
fingerprints. U17_FINGERPRINTS excludes itself. It fingerprints symbolic recipes as
printed, not expanded huge numbers. A ('sym',name) leaf is allowed only in declared
integer positions and resolves through U17_SYMBOLS; labels otherwise retain str/int
values, including distinction between 0 and '0'. No symbolic expression is evaluated.

A literal decimal/byte recipe is a tuple of literal ASCII strings and
('repeat',one_ASCII_character,nonnegative_count) parts; concatenate parts in order,
without substitutions, implicit spacing or newline. The listed LF is the actual byte
0a. T=10**4800 has 4,801 decimal digits, exceeding both test process limits 4,300/640.
All huge number tokens remain JSON numbers, never quoted numeric strings.

Preserve all 379 U15_INPUTS and 10 U16_INPUTS qualified identities, including aliases.
Add precisely seven U17_INPUTS entries. Every cumulative pass invokes 396 identities
under Standard and Accelerated, exactly 792 real global calls. No duplicate graph is
removed. These are NOT pytest case counts. Production certificate emission/verification
on every call is an obligatory Phase D/E test, not accomplished by this Phase C data.

## ORACLE-127 — Independent numerical references and endpoint witnesses

For every nonempty shore U independently compute s=f(U), e=e_q(U), b=b_q(U).
The least feasible total is 2 for s=1, 1 for positive even s, and 0 for odd s>=3.
The greatest is b if s+b is odd and b-1 otherwise. Keep only totals in [0,b] with
s+Y odd and >=3. Lem:interval realizes every total; the complete difference proof
shows an interior total cannot exceed both extremes. Enumerate all original shores
privately (increasing binary mask), then least/greatest totals, retaining strict
improvements, solely to choose the REFERENCE representative below. Greedily allocate
that total over crossing edges in canonical reference order. This reference rule is
NOT a solver tie rule and is NEVER imposed on either production selection.

On every registered graph with max q<=6 additionally enumerate every boundary-count
vector and every feasible scalar total, and cross-check both optima independently.
Larger multiplicities use finite all-shore endpoints, not q- or Q-copy enumeration.
These are finite exponential private oracles, not a production complexity claim.
U15_GLOBAL values are additionally cross-checked numerically, not replaced.

U17_GLOBALS fixes one raw reference pair and attaining witness per qualified entry.
Solver results may differ in witness/raw scale and must compare by cross multiplication.
The separate byte verifier does NOT consult this table or prove optimality: it accepts
any admissible literally attaining certificate, including the suboptimal fixtures.

## ORACLE-128 — Independent exact bytes and literal attainment

For each nonempty witness in U17_BYTES the defining raw integers are
N=2*(e+Y), D=s+Y-1, with odd s+Y>=3, bounded crossing counts and nonempty U.
U17_WITNESS_MATH lists (s,e,b,Y) independently summed from the primitive graph.
comparison_to_global is -1 for suboptimal, 0 for optimal; neither is part of the
certificate. Empty has no witness or sums and requires independently validated Q=1.

Source endpoints have Y=b,b-1,0,1,2 for L0,L1,H0,H1,H2 respectively. Baseline first
selects its lem:empty shore category, then applies the all/all-minus-one lem:unit
upgrade. Baseline categories even, odd>=3, unit degree>=2, matching and category/index
priority traps are explicit. ZERO retains (0,2), U=[0], y=[], not Empty (0,1).
INTERIOR is a valid nonendpoint: q=6,f=(3,3),Y=2, raw(4,4), below max(12,8).

L1-ZERO-OMIT uses original U=[0,1] in N-SEED002-GLOBAL: the first crossing unit
edge loses its only copy and disappears from sparse y; the surviving reference is 2.
SPARSE-GAP uses vertices 2 and 5, selecting references 2 and 4 with reference 3 omitted;
DISCONNECTED uses reference 3 on the later component. Neither refers to cut coordinates.
FULL/H0 have no selected boundary copies. Labels never occur in certificate bytes.

H2-ONE and H2-SPLIT are literal (4,2), selecting either one count of two or two counts
of one. H2-LOSER is attained but suboptimal. Direct H2 cannot be a strict final winner:
an even boundary gives the same value 2 as L0, and an odd boundary>=3 gives L1 value 2.
The complete preceding branch sweep thus already dominates/ties H2. Capture the actual
local reconstruction via test-local bindings, never edit the solver or invent a winner.

TIE-SMALL/TIE-LARGE on C020 legitimately attain (4,2) and (8,4) with different witnesses.
Their numeric equality does not allow attaching either pair to the unchanged OTHER
witness. Literal comparison is mandatory even for numerator zero. Repeated identical
inputs must produce the exact listed bytes; cross-route ties need not produce equal
bytes. No secondary minimizer, witness canonicalization or extra solve is permitted.

The recipes below are independently specified literals, never an encoder's output as
its own expected answer. Bytes include literal key/tag spelling, numeric token syntax,
fixed key/list order, no spaces/BOM, and exactly one final LF. Lengths and hashes bind
the complete expanded recipes. BIG-COUNTS carries N=D=2T-2 and selected T-1; BIG-ZERO
has (0,T); BIG-N has (2T,2); BIG-LABEL validates labels T,-T without encoding them in
the certificate. Fixed support, arbitrary encoded magnitude; no copy expansion.

## ORACLE-129 — Independent byte-only route and adversarial inputs

Private independent_wire.verify accepts ONLY (instance_bytes,certificate_bytes),
validates the complete canonical active instance FIRST, then certificate grammar,
then original U/edge references, admissibility and both literal raw equalities.
No exactfrac imports, production object, parser, serializer, validator, expected sums,
production witness helper or optimality flag enters that function. A fresh subprocess
blocks all exactfrac and exactfrac_verify imports, checks sys.modules, and exercises it
with only byte pairs. Phase D integrates a test-only implementation in the single new
test file; Unit 18 independently implements its own production decoder/checker later.

Instance JSON parsing is duplicate-decoded-key aware before dictionary collapse,
UTF-8 only, no BOM, exact signed integer tokens (labels may be negative), no -0,
fractions/exponents/nonfinite values or hidden decimal cutoff. Validate exact keys,
types/labels, positive q/f, sorted oriented unique edges, nonempty support and active
condition; never sort/aggregate/repair. Certificate parsing first matches its exact
lexical grammar; reordered/escaped/duplicate keys cannot match. Semantic checking
then recomputes s,e,Y and literal N,D; it does not re-encode the object as a grammar test.
MemoryError/resource failure remains operational and is not converted to invalid data.

Wire operations below act on the indicated stream starting with its base fixture.
'set'/'delete' use the exact path of dict keys/list indices; re-encode the mutated
primitive object in its existing key order, retaining the original terminal LF if any.
'replace' requires exactly one occurrence of the literal old UTF-8 bytes. 'prefix',
'suffix', 'prefix_hex', 'strip_final_lf', and 'reverse_keys' have their literal meanings.
'quote_field' quotes the whole unquoted nonnegative number token of that field.
'pretty' uses ordinary JSON object whitespace; 'utf8_strings' emits decoded non-ASCII
labels as UTF-8 instead of ASCII escapes. Mutation transport is not a validator or
production serializer. Every expanded bad/accepted stream is length/SHA-bound below.

Rejection reason families explain the targeted obligation, not stable production error
messages. The six equal_ratio cases are explicitly cross-multiplied before rejection.
C-ODD-TOO-SMALL keeps schema N=0,D=1 so the odd-total-1 minimum guard is reached before
literal denominator checking. C-EVEN-TOTAL uses total 4, with literal N=2,D=3, isolating
parity. Malformed bytes belong to the TEST-ONLY route now and Unit 18 later; Unit 17's
object serializer never decodes them or recovers duplicate keys erased by a caller.

## ORACLE-130 — Supported object boundary, dependency faults and precedence

The following are fixed future Unit 17 object-boundary fixtures, NOT a claim that
certificate.py exists or has passed them. All JSON-representable schema/math mutations
above also apply to the serializer object boundary except wire-only lexical/order
failures. Reversed DICT insertion order is ACCEPTED by the serializer and must emit
the same fixed bytes; descending U/y remains REJECTED, never repaired. Fresh independent
objects must serialize without a preceding build. Mutate a successful export into
C-WRONG-D and require revalidation; mutate U/y in one export and prove other outputs
and all closed records unchanged. Interleave dissimilar instances and both routes.

Argument recipe kinds identify test-local normally constructed values: None; primitive
graph dict; the exact bytes or decoded text of the base fixture; list(dict.items());
closed SolveResult; outer (SolveResult,SolveStats) tuple; subclasses made by normal
inherited construction; duck objects with matching attributes. No constructor bypass.
'retype' retains the value but substitutes the named exact-type trap. At 'format-key'
rebuild the dictionary with an actual str-subclass key (plain reassignment of an equal
key is insufficient). bool uses True; float uses the numerically equal float; Fraction
uses the equal rational; coercible-int is a local object with __int__ returning the
old integer. list-subclass/tuple contain the old members. normal-result means create
SolveResult(ExactValue(N,D),Witness(U_mask,dense_y)), or None for the witness; every
listed malformed graph-dependent record is shape-valid through its frozen constructors.

Validation order stays DESIGN 4.14.7: instance, outer result/object, exact-str keys and
format/empty presence, tag, bool, key set, N then D, then Empty or U/sparse y/Witness/
witness_value and literal raw comparison. Guard-isolate these stages with local spies;
do not infer precedence from a later unrelated failure. A dependency's raised exception
must be the identical object observed by the caller. Only explicitly detected wrong
normal-return promises raise RuntimeError; no broad exception translation or extra
forgery-validation domain. Wrong arity/frozen mutation retain Python/dataclass behavior.

## ORACLE-131 — Determinism, large-integer resources and executed-evidence boundary

Use fresh processes with PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 73 and with nonzero interpreter integer
conversion limits 4300 and 640. First establish the limit is active by an intentionally
failing whole-token conversion, then verify BIG-* inputs/bytes with the independent
bounded-seven-digit parser. Future production serialization must retain the setting,
not change it or rely on the caller disabling it. Replay all literal expectations in
both seeds; repeated identical inputs and reordered input dict keys yield identical
output bytes. Different tied solver results need only agree numerically.

No schema digit/byte quota is introduced. Actual host exhaustion is not invalid math.
Inject deterministic MemoryError at each declared dependency boundary instead of
exhausting resources. Later untrusted-file ingress must disclose its own external
budgets. Separate structural O(n+m) validation scans from output-sized storage and
integer conversion bit work; no universal timing/strong-operation certificate claim.

The private audit can additionally run the frozen global solver twice per graph AFTER
independent fixtures are fixed. Those observed results are transcribed with a private
transport encoder and verified in the independent audit process from the two byte
streams. They are explicitly closed-solver mathematical preflight, NOT Unit 17 emitted
certificates. Actual build/serialize for every run remains mandatory Phase D/E.
Every final run preserves its OWN raw pair, not this catalogue's representative pair.
Local Baseline/L0/L1/H0/H1/H2 candidate captures are counted separately from final results.
No run is added just to force tie equality; no source is edited by those observers.

U17_MUTATIONS preregisters production detectors. Phase C executes byte adversaries and
may test mutants of the private oracle itself, but reports these SEPARATELY; it cannot
claim successful mutation testing of an absent production module. CE19 still requires
executed production faults after GREEN. External/second-model review remains optional.

## ORACLE-132 — Inventory, fingerprints and controlled continuation

The counts below are independently fixed fixture/registry counts. They are not the
number of future pytest cases. Count actual parsing, rejection, comparison and solver
executions separately in each audit output. No phantom corpus entry is created from a
malformed instance, dependency fault or metadata-only scenario. Every valid additional
graph is registered above; reuse of inherited graph fixtures preserves its identity.
After oracle-only application, audit/regression/Ruff, review, staging, local commit,
postcommit checks and remote closure, Phase D may create tests/test_certificate.py.
It must fail specifically for missing exactfrac.certificate. Until then that test,
exactfrac/certificate.py and exactfrac_verify/check.py remain absent. No Unit 18 gate,
production decoding API, current-unit conformance promotion or private-note check.

## ORACLE-135 — Serialized acceptance/rejection and exact consumption

Rows reference U17/<literal id> or U18/<literal id>. Apply ops to one stream only. Inherited ops
retain ORACLE-129 semantics; truncate(k) takes the first k bytes; encoding(name) changes UTF8 text
encoding; raw_hex supplies literal bytes; replace_hex requires one exact match. Each resulting
stream has independently computed byte length/SHA. Good=False requires exact ValueError in
future production; reason is explanatory and does not prescribe diagnostic prose.
Every inherited 140 rejection and seven acceptance rows is still required independently. All
strict prefixes of representative full and Empty certificates are registered as truncation errors.
Y-RENUMBER deliberately ACCEPTS a different but admissible witness with the same total: not every
coordinate or instance change is invalid. GRAPH-CHANGE-RAW and GRAPH-CHANGE-F isolate changes
which do invalidate the structural pair. Metadata-only changes cannot create unique binding.
Escaped unpaired surrogates remain valid inherited string labels; raw invalid UTF8 does not.
PAIR-RESCALE-UP, PAIR-REDUCE, ZERO-NORMALIZE and six inherited forgeries preserve numerical ratio
but fail literal attainment. PARITY-ISOLATED has total 4, N=2,D=3. MINIMUM-ISOLATED has total 1
with schema-valid N=0,D=1 so its minimum predicate precedes the unavoidable raw-D mismatch.

### Interpretation and derivation boundaries

Human-readable literal tables below are the committed fixture authority. The
private JSON mirror is redundant transport and is checked against every table.
Cells are Python literals; symbols and inherited byte recipes keep their earlier
meaning. U19 byte recipes additionally allow ('hex', lowercase_hex) for deliberately
malformed UTF-8 or valid non-ASCII spellings. A repeat run encodes the specified
ASCII character that many times; no production encoder defines expected bytes.

U19_ARGV gives complete token vectors and independently transcribed normal
returns/stream outcomes. EMITTED_CERTIFICATE means the already checked emitter
bytes, not an expected witness guessed from a solver. Grammar acceptances presume
that selected input acquisition and dependency calls subsequently succeed. Python
call-type failures are separate from ordinary grammar returns. Expected failure
tracebacks and interpreter-level numeric failure statuses are not frozen.

U19_INSTANCE_SYNTAX specifies new input encodings, not new mathematical graph
identities. Valid variants refer to inherited ordered graphs, including exact
labels, and record their independently decoded canonical transport fingerprint.
The categories syntax/schema/unsupported correspond respectively to the private
syntax adapter, closed Instance.from_dict malformed-data rejection, and its active
condition rejection. These categories do not authorize broad exception catches.
All operationally injected exceptions keep identity. The syntax cases are derived
from 4.16.6 and 4.1A, not discovered by asking the proposed CLI for its verdict.

All 400 inherited qualified graph identities and all 519 fixed byte pairs remain
mandatory. Mathematical duplicate inputs are not deduplicated. The 41 inherited
literal recipes retain their original field ordering, raw N,D, U and sparse edge
references. The independent reference recomputes sums and admissibility from bytes;
exhaustive tiny-shore endpoint values cross-check the finite input registry.

U19_SOLVE_RESULT_SEAMS uses the already fixed literal witnesses as supplied return
values of a test-local solver seam. In particular zero and losing H2 witnesses are
not claims about a real final optimum. The exact bytes are inherited by recipe and
hash. Actual real-solver final output is compared by literal raw preservation to
its own captured SolveResult and numerically against independent graph references.
Different legal witnesses/raw pairs across routes under ties remain permitted.

Stream plans constrain ordered events, not an additional import-order rule beyond
complete grammar validation first. File acquisition precedes checker validation:
an unreadable second file wins over an already read but malformed first file.
Write failures can leave a prefix; no atomic stdout or rollback claim is made.
Descriptors of bad return values/exceptions are prospective test-local seam
injections, not production execution performed by this catalogue audit.

Independent oracle checks and closed-dependency preflight run before any CLI.
Every future CLI fault is preregistered, not counted as a killed production mutant.
No private reference is a future production parser or a replacement checker.

## Unit 20 Phase C — independent oracle registration for unit20-v1

**Classification:** `GLOBAL_ORACLE`, `CROSS_MODEL_EQUIVALENCE`, and separately
identified engineering/negative fixtures. Adopted source: canonical V2.2,
`def:instance`, `ass:active`, `def:parameter`, `lem:aggregation`, `lem:interval`,
`prop:expanded-equivalence`, `lem:empty`, `lem:endpoint-difference`, and
`prop:endpoints`. `def:complexities` and `thm:main` supply the scope boundary,
not a finite-test complexity conclusion.

Engineering authority is DESIGN D20-C1--D20-C10, D20-M1--D20-M3 and TEST_PLAN
CP1--CP18, at commit `a3d15b96d8aa8aa903648ce140af54b37bb481ab`, tree
`2c6fc287203d51c4f2a405ded48ec878bdd6dad4`. This appendix preserves the complete
3,392,373-byte catalogue prefix, SHA-256
`523e3025e53fc1676ccd60a8e3e1f1955a8ace545ec34fea0cf4fa5d59dd056b`.
Earlier tables and their fingerprints are unchanged.

### Independence and exact meaning

Expected inputs, bytes, and optima are fixed here before `exactfrac/corpus.py`,
`tests/test_corpus.py`, or any owned payload exists in the repository. Two private
stdlib-only derivations were written from the authority prose. A builds the grid
with direct support lists and a base-10^9 codec; B independently reconstructs IDs,
uses pair predicates for supports and a base-1000 codec, and strictly parses tokens
in at most six-digit chunks. Neither imports ExactFrac, its verifier, its tests,
its serializers, or an optimizer. Agreement of two implementations supplements,
not replaces, the following mathematical derivation. Companion JSON and scripts
are private evidence; the committed human tables and byte registration govern.

For each nonempty shore U set s=f(U), e=e_q(U), b=b_q(U). The admissible total
interval is the parity subsequence of [max(0,3-s), b] with s+x odd. By
`lem:interval`, every integer total in [0,b] is attained by compact boundary
counts. Let l be its smallest admissible total and h its largest. There is no
admissible selection for that shore when l>h. Otherwise evaluate

    N(x)=2(e+x), D(x)=s+x-1, x in {l,h} (one evaluation if l=h).

Every denominator is positive. The direct two-step difference has sign s-e-1:

    R(x+2)-R(x) = 4(s-e-1) / ((s+x+1)(s+x-1)).

Thus an endpoint attains the shore optimum. A enumerates masks 1..2^n-1 and both
extreme totals in increasing order; B enumerates vertex combinations and chooses
the extreme from that difference sign. Both enumerate all nonempty shores,
without using production branch transformations, parity cuts, or branch solvers.
For huge multiplicities neither scans 0..Q, boundary count ranges, or expanded
copies. The independent reference is finite/exponential in n; it is not a
strongly polynomial solver implementation.

For each of the 379 microinstances, independently enumerate every compact boundary
count vector, every scalar total, and every subset of the individually labelled
boundary copies (Q<=6). Compare attainable admissible-total sets and each shore's
optimum against the endpoints. The number of expanded subsets mapping to vector
y is independently checked as the product of binomial(q_j,y_j). This checks
copy multiplicity semantics rather than treating a support edge as indivisible.
Only `edge-q01-f01-01` is Empty. Other locally zero quotients are not Empty.

Every nonempty row records one attaining reference shore and total. Reconstruct
its count vector by filling boundary edges in increasing canonical edge_ref
order, using min(remaining total,q_j), and zero on the remaining boundary edges.
All that total is consumed. This specifies a reference witness, not a required
tie choice for either production route. Compare any later returned value by
positive-denominator cross multiplication; do not require the same raw pair,
mask, boundary counts, or witness on tied values. Empty rows have marker True,
pair (0,1), mask 0, Y=0, and no witness.

### Numeric-expression and construction legend

In a row with bits>=64, **T=2^(bits-2)** for that row only. A token such as
`12*T+15` is exactly that integer; `T`, multiplication by a small nonnegative
integer, and one signed small integer constant are the only symbolic forms.
All other numeric tokens are ordinary bounded decimal integers. In bits<64
rows all values are literal. In micro rows bits=0 is a table marker, not a
multiplicity-width claim. No float, tolerance, reduced-fraction requirement,
full-token huge-int conversion, or interpreter-limit change is involved.

The recipe ID fixes the complete construction under D20-C3--C6. Edge micro q/f
and triangle slots/f are literal in the ID; zero triangle slots are absent.
Nonmicro supports are registered below in canonical edge order. Structural q
is flat: q_j=2^bits-1. Bit-sweep q uses its declared flat/ramp mode with seed 0.
Seeded q is ramp with its explicit seed. Ramp means
2^(bits-1)+((j+seed) mod 2^(bits-1)), after final support sorting. The complete
weighted degree and capacity vectors are independently recorded in every row.
Capacity formulas remain unit=1, half=ceil(d/2), near=max(1,d-1), degree=d,
and alternating=1 at even dense vertex indices and d at odd indices.

Owned path is relative to instances/. Every payload is compact ASCII JSON with
ordered keys format,n,edges,f, format exactfrac-instance/1, canonical support,
unquoted ordinary integer tokens, and exactly one LF. No labels or extra fields.
The independent length and SHA-256 below fix the resulting bytes, not merely a
self-emitted checksum. Equal bytes under distinct IDs are intentionally retained.

### Preregistered adversarial and rejection families

These are **future detection obligations, not executed production mutants**.
A guard-isolated fault requires a pristine passing control and a changed case
reaching the intended assertion; an earlier unrelated rejection is insufficient.
Production faults must later use actual generator interventions. Filesystem,
aggregate, cross-route and preservation interventions are separately classified
as integration/transition controls. Source inspection alone is not execution.

### Phase and claim boundaries

This Phase C package appends only docs/ORACLE_CATALOG.md. It does not populate
instances/MANIFEST, create corpus.py or test_corpus.py, edit tests/test_cli.py,
change CONFORMANCE, run experiments, release anything, or inspect private notes.
The CLI test remains 99,918 bytes with its full original Unit 19 R2 identity.
The exact 94-byte MANIFEST-pin retirement is Phase D only. No new enduring
pin on a future-mutable artifact is introduced. Historical phase-local ledgers
are evidence, not repository tests.

All 655 independent endpoint values, all 379 cross-model micro checks, and the
initial-byte identities are preregistered. Later owning tests must independently
parse/validate generated payloads and the live aggregate, preserve the Unit 20
projection through legitimate extension, and compare actual Standard/Accelerated
outputs on the declared 384 inputs (768 solves). The independent checker proves
admissibility and attainment, not optimality; these finite endpoint comparisons
supply the latter for this declared set. There is no claim of solving all 655
with production, universal correctness, strong polynomiality from finite tests,
practical scalability, timings, look-ahead coverage, or release readiness.

## Unit 21 independent experiment oracle fixtures — U21-OR1

Status: Phase C preregistration, prior to consuming tests and experiment production.
The governing authority is DESIGN §14 D21-E1–D21-E16 and TEST_PLAN §47 EP1–EP20,
remotely closed in 4fe522e0283a39ae773e2cb27cd5f1b8be410d81.
No preceding catalogue byte is changed. These are finite reference expectations,
not a record of running the initial experiment campaign and not a theorem promotion.

### Provenance and representation

The Unit 20 independent input/optimum table remains the mathematical reference.
Its 655 identities, including the 599 byte-distinct payloads, are not deduplicated.
The inherited independent reference A reconstructs those inputs from D20 rules;
independent reference B rechecks the inputs, exact endpoint optima and all 379
microinstances by compact vectors, scalar totals and expanded-copy subsets.
Neither uses an ExactFrac solver or the future experiment implementation.
The complete input-summary bank below adds only the D21-E9 bit-width proxy,
original recipe index and the existing exact optimum expressions.
For expression_bits B>=64, T means 2^(B-2) in that row. Smaller literal integers
retain their meanings. No full-token conversion of enormous integers is required.

The canonical source definitions def:instance, ass:active and def:parameter govern
admissibility and density; lem:empty distinguishes the valid Q=1 Empty case.
The distinction in def:complexities and thm:main is not proved by these fixtures.
Field names are independently inspected from the already-closed record classes,
not learned from a future serializer. Their file identities are recorded below.
The computations here are separate reference constructions by the same build
assistant, not an unrecorded external review or a separate-model endorsement.

### Schedule expectations, not observed invocations

For even i the two-route orders at r=-1,0,1,2 are AS, SA, AS, SA.
For odd i the orders are SA, AS, SA, AS. A means Accelerated; S means Standard.
All indices are those of the entire ASCII-sorted 655-recipe registry, even when a
small synthetic fixture extracts a subset. Measured rounds are 0,1,2; warmup has
round -1 and wire repeat 0. SCHEDULE.tsv fixes all scheduled identities, not calls.

### Exact schemas, source paths and constant strings

FIELD_REGISTRY fixes nine already-closed dataclass field lists. W is the ordered
25 WorkStats fields. Its first 20 fields are summed across branch/nonbranch buckets;
the final five are maxima. Diagnostic values are NOT summed across repeated trials.
BranchOracleStats.max_flow_calls is a computed property, not an eighth native key.
AlgorithmStats.branch_solver and attaining_branch are computed properties, not
extra algorithm keys. Standard/Accelerated native field sets remain distinct.

WIRE_SCHEMAS fixes the explicit wire field sets and expanded CSV headers from
D21-E9/E10/E12. It introduces no public decoder/encoder API. E3 specifies fixed
non-echoing usage behavior but not a complete literal help/usage sentence; this
oracle does not invent an additional exact-message requirement.

The source fingerprint fixture uses the actual 20 closed source-file hashes and
TWO COMMENT-ONLY SYNTHETIC placeholders for the not-yet-existing experiment module
and wrapper. The placeholders are fixture strings, not repository files, not a
production implementation, and not the final campaign code identity. The ordered
22-entry identity is hashed using E8's NUL/LF framing; the binary fixture is shown
as base64 solely to preserve its NUL bytes. An output path does not enter this hash.
A runtime source fingerprint must be measured from actual source bytes later.

SYNTHETIC_RUN_INFO contains explicitly synthetic platform/interpreter labels and
a fake clock description. Its protocol strings and schemas are exact E10 constants.
Its inputs.recipes=655 specifies the adopted campaign, not evidence that the small
row subset executed it. Its source hash binds only the disclosed fixture sources.
Finite environmental floats are example spellings, not cross-machine measurements.

### Small scripted record and table fixture

All diagnostic work and times in this bank are SYNTHETIC. Each of three real tiny
input identities supplies one fake warmup and three fake measured calls per route:
24 scripted records = 6 warmups + 18 measured records. These are independent data,
not outputs from running an experiment module, which does not yet exist.
The exact subset tables have 6 summary rows, 16 branch rows and 3 comparison rows.
The real tiny certificate witnesses below establish independent admissibility and
literal attainment; a closed checker may validate them without a solver call.

| Recipe | Route | Measured nanoseconds (synthetic, in repeat order) | Median |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| edge-q01-f01-01 | Standard | 13, 3, 7 | 7 |
| edge-q01-f01-01 | Accelerated | 19, 0, 5 | 5 |
| struct-cycle-n04-b00001-fdegree | Standard | 90, 4, 21 | 21 |
| struct-cycle-n04-b00001-fdegree | Accelerated | 55, 9, 18 | 18 |
| tri-q1-1-1-f1-1-1 | Standard | 88, 6, 20 | 20 |
| tri-q1-1-1-f1-1-1 | Accelerated | 77, 2, 15 | 15 |

Every main median differs from its first sample and arithmetic mean. Warmups are
null and make no clock reads; the measured zero remains zero. Separate timing
vectors include repeated values and zero medians. Scripted positive clock values
and their paired differences are prescribed solely for interval spies.

On the unit-capacity triangle the full shore has N/D=6/2. On the degree-capacity
four-cycle the Standard fixture chooses U={0}, y_0=1 giving 2/2, whereas the
Accelerated fixture chooses U={0,1}, y_1=1 giving 4/4. These distinct admissible raw
pairs have equal quotients, but neither may be normalized while retaining its old
literal witness. They are NOT a prediction of either solver's actual tie choice.
The Empty single-copy input has exactly (0,1), no branches and no fake witness.

Each nonempty synthetic Standard trace has branch oracle counts 2,4,3,1 and
outer counts 1,3,2,0. The last branch is infeasible and still appears in the table.
Each nonempty synthetic Accelerated trace has branch oracle counts 2,7,6,1.
Branch 0 is an initialization return; branch 1 has one accepted and one rejected
look-ahead followed by Newton termination; branch 2 has accepted look-ahead then
look-ahead termination; branch 3 is infeasible. Per-trace total look-ahead queries
are 4 = 2 accepted + 1 rejected + 1 terminal. The record constructor checks the
native/count algebra, not the occurrence of those paths on these inputs.

The small synthetic nonbranch peaks 70,80,90 dominate the relevant branch peaks.
A separate giant-row fixture puts 10^4400+17 in a native flow maximum, producing
4401 decimal digits, flow_peak_bits=14617 and whole peak 14620. It is a codec and
max-aggregation trap, not a claim that the tiny input generates that integer.
The entire-token integer limit remains unchanged; this fixture is audited at 640.
No timing comparison, speedup, hypothesis verdict or memory claim follows.

### Phase boundary

Only this catalogue appendix is the repository change in Phase C. All source,
consuming tests, corpus data, DESIGN, TEST_PLAN, SPEC_LOCK, CONTRACT and CONFORMANCE
remain at their closed identities. The future experiment module, direct wrapper,
experiment test and initial results directory remain absent. No experiment campaign,
result table from measured execution, release, or new theorem status is created.
Oracle staging, local commit, postcommit checks and remote closure remain separate;
only after that closure may the consuming tests-first RED phase begin.


## Unit 21B — Phase C independent irregular oracle, R1

**Scope.** This appendix registers expectations under DESIGN D21B-I1–I16 and
TEST_PLAN IR1–IR24 before either sibling production module or its consuming test
exists. It adds no gate or interface. The 960 s-token main recipes and 240 p-token
pilot recipes are distinct identities in suite `unit21-v2`. The historical
`unit21-v1` campaign and all earlier catalogue bytes are preserved.

### Derivation and claim boundaries

All 1,200 input byte strings, capacities, support fingerprints and descriptor
geometry records were derived separately twice, without importing a production
generator or solver. Reference A visits nonempty shores in increasing mask order
and evaluates the least and greatest admissible scalar boundary totals, equal
endpoints once. Reference B visits Gray-code shores and uses the independently
coded monotonic-extreme reduction. Each examines exactly 20,984,400 shores;
20,983,790 are feasible and 610 infeasible. A evaluates 41,966,731 endpoints;
B evaluates 20,983,790 monotonic extremes. Counts are definition-level reference
work, not production telemetry, backend execution or complexity evidence.

For all 200 preregistered b=1, n in {6,8} recipes (160 main, 40 pilot), two
literal compact-vector implementations (C++ and portable standard-library
Python) each visited 475,407,622 vectors, of which 237,703,285 were admissible.
Their full per-recipe results and first-attaining witnesses agree byte-for-byte;
all 200 optima agree with both endpoint references. An independent polynomial
coefficient count additionally checks the vector census; it is NOT described
as enumeration. The 200-vector subset is not a production-solve preview.

Raw optimum pairs below are unreduced attainment pairs. Numerical equality is
positive-denominator cross multiplication, not structural equality. A and B
may retain different first-attaining shores or raw pairs because their
enumeration orders differ. Neither a C0 certificate nor finite testing alone
proves universal correctness, strong polynomiality, asymptotic growth, a
practical n-limit, or speedup.

### Registered schedules, schemas and synthetic controls

MAIN_SCHEDULE has exactly 7,680 positions: 1,920 warmups (round -1, repeat 0)
and 5,760 measured calls (round/repeat 0,1,2). PILOT_SCHEDULE has 480 positions
at round/repeat 0. These are required positions, NOT performed solves.
The exact 25 source paths consist of the 22 closed D21-E8 paths and the three
I1 siblings. Three nonexecutable placeholder byte strings are used solely in
SYNTHETIC_SOURCE_IMAGES to exercise fingerprint framing. They are not
implementation files, and cannot establish a future source identity.

Every file whose name or kind says SYNTHETIC, every boundary H5/H3 example, and
the whole SYNTHETIC_WIRE_BANK.zip are ARTIFICIAL fixtures: no actual solver
call, clock measurement, pilot observation or main campaign outcome is used.
The full wire bank contains both complete protocol examples with their exact
byte ledgers. It is compressed only to avoid repeating large nested telemetry
records throughout this document. SYNTHETIC_WIRE_BANK_INDEX enumerates all
uncompressed entries; decode the base64 fence, open the ZIP without path
extraction, and verify each length/hash. Human-readable projections and complete
synthetic findings/coverage tables are shown separately. Projections do not
authorize subset execution. Only actual Phase E records may support paper claims.

Synthetic records exercise all 25 WorkStats fields, sum-of-events versus
maximum-of-peaks, solve-level H2 carriers, source/input/certificate binding,
zero elapsed time, alternate pilot cell intervals, exact 4,401-digit tokens,
escaped text, mixed wins/ties/losses, 23/24-cell and pooled-median boundaries,
untestable H5, negative half-medians, H3 route separation and tied slopes.
H3 arithmetic examples test the separately registered paper estimator; no
H3 slope appears in a production unit table. TINY_CERTIFICATE_CASES includes
an admissible suboptimal C0, distinguishing attainment from global optimality,
and equal-value raw-pair/tied-witness cases.

FAULT_DECLARATIONS fixes 143 independently named fault families and their
intended guards. Each demands a passing pristine control and isolation of the
target defect from unrelated earlier guards. These are prospective Phase D/E
obligations, NOT 143 executed production mutants. Phase C fixture-auditor
mutations and later actual producer mutants must be reported separately.

No pilot was executed, no F7 date was supplied, and no main campaign is
authorized by this appendix. Pilot review and the author's freeze remain
required before main measurements. Private planning files are not gates.
